properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 5 at 6:55AM CDT until August 5 at 8:00AM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
SVREAX

The National Weather Service in Pleasant Hill has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Adair County in northeastern Missouri...
Northeastern Sullivan County in north central Missouri...
Putnam County in north central Missouri...
Schuyler County in northeastern Missouri...

* Until 800 AM CDT.

* At 654 AM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 6 miles north of Unionville to 8 miles northwest of
Green City to near Milan, moving east at 45 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Kirksville, Milan, Unionville, Lancaster, Green City, Queen City,
Novinger, Greentop, Downing, Greencastle, Brashear, Glenwood,
Gibbs, Pollock, Worthington, Livonia, Lemons, and Green Castle.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.
properties.area: Adair, MO; Putnam, MO; Schuyler, MO; Sullivan, MO

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued August 5 at 7:40AM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Coastal waters from Cape Fear NC to Little River Inlet SC out 20
NM...
Coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear NC out 20 nm...
Waters from Little River Inlet SC to South Santee River SC from 20
to 60 NM...
Waters from Surf City NC to Little River Inlet SC from 20 to 60
NM...

At 740 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. These thunderstorms were
located along a line extending from near Wr4 to 12 nm southeast of
Sunset Mid Shelf Buoy, moving southeast at 25 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until these storms pass. If caught on the open water,
prepare for deteriorating conditions. Make sure you and your crew are
wearing properly fitted life jackets.

These storms may produce a waterspout. A Special Marine Warning may
be needed.
properties.area: Coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear NC out 20 nm; Coastal waters from Cape Fear NC to Little River Inlet SC out 20 NM; Waters from Surf City NC to Little River Inlet SC from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Little River Inlet SC to South Santee River SC from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued August 5 at 9:13PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Guam Coastal Waters...
Rota Coastal Waters...

* At 913 PM ChST, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. These strong
thunderstorms were located along a line from 40 NM north of
Ritidian Buoy to 28 NM northwest of Ritidian Buoy, moving southeast
at 35 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Northern Guam and western Rota waters.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.

These thunderstorms will likely produce winds to around 30 knots, and
could pose a serious hazard for boaters. A Special Marine Warning may
eventually be required when these storms reach the nearshore waters.
Boaters should consider heading for shore before the storm arrives.
properties.area: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 8:07PM CDT until August 6 at 8:10PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 32.0 feet, The Nueces River backs up minor creeks to
near the slab elevation of homes in the River Creek Acres
Subdivision, five miles southeast of George West. Livestock are cut
off and could drown in low areas of the flood plain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 33.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 9.0 feet Sunday evening.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 3:54PM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 348 PM AKDT, The river gauge at the Yentna River at Lake
Creek indicates rises in water levels from heavy rain across
the warned area. Flooding is ongoing. Trees and debris larger
than telephone poles have been observed flowing down the
river. Between 1.0 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible
with higher amounts possible in the upper Yentna Basin.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 7:51am the stage was 20.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest slightly above 22 feet late tonight and
into early Wednesday morning.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 8:45AM AKDT until August 5 at 5:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Petersville Area

* WHEN...Until 500 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 842 AM AKDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain across the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Between 2 and 3 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to
1.5 inches are possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued August 3 at 11:03AM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from good to moderate, but is forecasted to degrade.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM Wednesday, August 5, 2026.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007
